references.text: The Lord predicts that Pharaoh will not let Israel go, and that He will strike Egypt with His wonders—this is the earlier prophecy fulfilled in Exodus 7:4.
The Lord promises to deliver Israel from Egypt with a mighty hand and great judgments, the same theme as in 7:4.
The Lord tells Moses that Pharaoh will not listen to them, so that the Lord's wonders may be multiplied in Egypt—a direct parallel to Pharaoh's hardness of heart in 7:4.
Fulfillment of the promise in 7:4—all the hosts of the Lord went out of Egypt.
The Lord brought the children of Israel out of Egypt, host by host—the fulfillment of the deliverance mentioned in 7:4.
Moses recalls that God took for Himself a people from the midst of another nation, with trials, signs, wonders, and great and terrible deeds—a reflection on the judgments in 7:4.
The Lord performed great and terrible signs and wonders against Egypt and Pharaoh—referring to the great judgments in 7:4.
The Lord brought Israel out of Egypt with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, with great and terrible deeds, signs, and wonders—a parallel to God's hand and judgments in 7:4.
Stephen's speech mentions that Moses led the people out and performed wonders and signs in Egypt—a New Testament reference to the events prophesied in Exodus 7:4.
Direct fulfillment: 3:20 is the prophecy about the hand and the wonders, which 7:4 shows as accomplished action.
Promise and fulfillment: 6:1 promises a 'strong hand,' and 7:4 shows how this hand was laid upon Egypt.
